basis: PXE affects elastic tissue in skin, retina and arterial walls; extent varies in forme fruste disease. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Premature loss of ovarian endocrine function; later osteoporosis and cardiovascular disease are separate conditions.
Congenital focal abnormality of the retinal pigment epithelium in the macula.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by pili torti, alopecia and sensorineural deafness. Nonspecific eye abnormalities do not establish functional damage; hypogonadism and ID are under 30%.
Hereditary motor neuropathy; distal muscle wasting results from denervation rather than a primary muscle disease.
ID and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; dental/palatal defects ~33-50%, hearing loss 33%. Strabismus 31% omitted by cap; neonatal hypoglycemia alone does not establish persistent endocrine damage.
Autoimmune inflammation of the uvea; the ENT ancestry does not establish airway or ear involvement.
Carcinoma originates in the glottis, part of the laryngeal airway.
Benign myofibroblastic connective-tissue neoplasm. Site varies; the breast-specific subtype has no anatomical axis.
Congenital focal dermal defects define the group; extracutaneous abnormalities are subtype-dependent and not established in most patients.
Heterogeneous single-organ disorder: bronchiectasis and pancreatitis define pulmonary and GI forms, respectively; isolated vas deferens disease has no axis. These sites need not coexist.
Malignant cartilage-forming mesenchymal tumor occurring in children; metastatic sites are not defining organs.
Luteinized ovarian stromal cells produce excess androgens, causing endocrine dysfunction. Associated hypertension does not establish direct vascular damage.
Factor V isoform disorder impairs blood coagulation and causes bleeding.
Renal, cerebellar and thyroid disease define syndrome; thrombocytopenia 30-79%. Hearing loss and muscle abnormalities, also 30-79%, omitted by cap.
Fibroblastic malignancy arising predominantly in deep soft tissues. Possible lung and bone metastases do not establish common involvement.
Defined by a speckled lentiginous nevus and cutaneous capillary malformation; neurologic or ocular damage is not established in most patients.
Personality disorder without a defining disease process in any of the 13 organ axes.
Hereditary diffuse cerebral disease with dementia and spastic paraplegia; hearing impairment and blindness lack evidence of frequency or anatomical localization.
Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with epilepsy and frequent structural brain abnormalities; ocular and skeletal abnormalities are under 30%.
Neoplasm located in the cornea.
Mature B-cell lymphoma warrants blood-cell and lymphoma mechanism axes; its breast site has no anatomical axis.
Inherited epilepsy spectrum; generalized seizures are very frequent. No additional organ damage is established across the group.
Paraneoplastic calcium dysregulation. Delirium and altered cardiovascular function do not establish persistent organ injury; hematologic ancestry alone does not imply blood-cell disease.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define syndrome; ptosis 80-99% and tracheal sleeve 20/20 support eye and airway involvement. Airway estimate may reflect a selected cohort.
